chunks: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Yahya al-Attar (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd b. Abdullah narrated to us from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Isa from his father from Muhammad b. Abi Umayr from Ali b. Abi Hamza from Abu Basir from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad from his forefathers from Ali (peace be upon them all). He said:

The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said: Indeed, in Paradise there are rooms whose outside can be seen from their inside, and whose inside can be seen from their outside. Those of my community who purified their speech, fed people food, spread peace, and prayed at night while people slept will inhabit them.

So Ali (peace be upon him) said: O Messenger of God, and who from your community is able to do this? He said: O Ali, do you not know what purification of speech is? It is whoever says, when they awake and when they go to sleep, 'Glory be to God, and praise be to God, and there is no god but God, and God is the Greatest' ten times. And feeding people food is the expenditure of a man on his family. As for praying at night while people are asleep: whoever prays Maghrib, the final Isha, and the morning prayer in the mosque in congregation, it is as though he kept vigil all night. And spreading peace is not being stingy in greeting every single Muslim with the salaam.

key_terms.أحيا الليل: Kept vigil all night; revived the night through worship
key_terms.إطابة الكلام: Purification of speech; here explained as dhikr rather than eloquence
key_terms.إفشاء السلام: Spreading the greeting of peace (salaam) among Muslims
key_terms.غرف: Rooms, chambers; elevated rooms in Paradise reserved for the righteous

ai.seo_question: What are the four qualities that earn rooms in Paradise according to the Prophet Muhammad?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) described special transparent rooms in Paradise for those who fulfill four qualities. When Imam Ali (AS) asked who could manage such demanding conditions, the Prophet explained each one in practical, attainable terms: purifying speech means reciting the four praises (tasbih, tahmid, tahlil, takbir) morning and evening; feeding people means providing for one's own family; night prayer means performing the obligatory prayers in the mosque in congregation; and spreading peace means not withholding the greeting of salaam from any Muslim.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on him
